ADIOS is a probabilistic, context-free grammar that learns from unannotated corpora by means of a context-sensitive generalization procedure. 2.1 Pattern significance The first step in ADIOS is the inference of patterns in a corpus, that is, the detection of the recurring syntactic structures in a set of sentences.

ADIOS is a system that learns the structure of a natural language from unannotated corpora, by using a combination of the following techniques: (a) a context-sensitive probabilistic inference of patterns from the corpus, (b) a generalization of the inferred patterns to more complex patterns by means of a context-sensitive grammar, (c) an automatic construction of a grammar that describes the patterns, and (d) an efficient parsing of new text with the constructed grammar. 1 Rich Syntax

ADIOS is a system for the automatic extraction and generalization of context-sensitive patterns from a corpus of unannotated text, and that it can be applied to any corpus of natural language, including speech, and any language. 1 The name “DIOS” was suggested by the late Professor Noam Chomsky.
